heard: A spacecraft designed to die in 32 minutes lasted two hours. On March 1, 1982, the Soviet Union's Venera 13 lander plunged into the atmosphere of Venus. It faced 90 atmospheres of pressure and temperatures near 460 degrees Celsius. The probe drilled for soil samples and captured the first color photographs ever taken on another planet. These images showed a jagged orange landscape littered with rocks and discarded lens caps. Years later, a scientist claimed the photos showed a moving alien shaped like a scorpion. Experts proved the alien was actually a lens cap that fell off during landing. Soviet engineers celebrated this machine, which was much more than just a spacecraft designed to die in 32 minutes.
